cells.tense: You are here in the open with the pen, and the direction you picked is holding.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: A pull will come that wants you off your heading. Don't take it and don't argue with it — stay on the line you chose, once, plainly, and notice what it costs to stay.
cells.core:
The clearing has done its work. What was built on a premise that couldn't hold has come down, and what's left is simpler: a direction you actually chose, and a life that can move along it. You can tell the difference now between a pull that asks you to follow and a pull that only wants your attention. That difference is the skill. A pull doesn't become yours by feeling strong.

Holding the heading is the work, not remaking the choice. Something will tug at you, and the ask is to stay on the line without pushing back hard — simply not moving. One time is enough. Notice what it costs and what it doesn't. You'll know more after that one time than after a week of talking it through.
cells.sheetLine: The clearing is done. Holding the direction is now the work.

cells.tense: You're bracing for the next clearing before the last one has finished landing.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: After the next piece of work is finished, stop there. Don't scan for what else might be false. Let what the work already produced stand, untouched, before you move on to anything.
cells.core:
The clearing worked. What couldn't hold has fallen away. And already you're leaning into the next one — what else in your life might be false, what else might come down, what this connection could mean a year from now the way it hasn't meant anything yet. The future keeps arriving in your head before the present has had a chance to land.

The ground you're on is what the clearing left. After the next thing you do — one piece of work, one conversation — stop. Don't check whether it was the right thing. Don't hunt for the next false structure. What's actually here won't ask you to defend it. What asks for defense is the future, and it can wait until it isn't the future anymore.
cells.sheetLine: The clearing happened. Let what it left be enough for now.
cells.verb: choosing which stream to flow with
cells.place: where the false structure has just come down

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed and cleared an hour ago.
cells.act: sort the kinds of pull from one another
cells.ask: Set out the things pulling at you in a line. Beside each, mark whether it's yours or borrowed — one word, no reasoning — and follow the one marked yours until something proves it wrong.
cells.core:
The clearing happened, and you're not in it. You're still at the door of what fell — what it meant, what else could have been, whether you heard it right — while the room behind you is already empty and lighter. The connection that came through is real; you're just not standing where it landed.

Sorting the pulls is the way back. Three is enough. Set down what's pulling at you and mark which of them you actually chose and which you picked up somewhere else. Then act on the one that's yours. Not because it's the right one — because acting on something you chose is how the present gets weight again. You'll know it's yours because you won't need to argue for it.
cells.sheetLine: The door is behind you. Walk through the one you're standing in.

cells.tense: You're drawing the way through for someone while standing inside a passage you found yourself.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: When someone tells you they're stuck somewhere you've already been, give them the route you took — plain, short, no offer to walk it with them. Whatever they do with it belongs to them.
cells.core:
Something fell apart for you, the truth cleared the field, and the way through showed itself. You found it by walking it. Now someone nearby is standing where you stood, and you can see their way out as plainly as you saw your own. Telling them is real work, and when you tell it afterward you tell it like you happened to be standing there.

Pointing to the passage is what you're doing. Just the route you took, no walkthrough, no watching how it lands. A guide and a bystander differ only in that the guide knows they're guiding. Your finding it by accident doesn't make the finding less yours.
cells.sheetLine: You know the way through this. That knowing is yours.

attempts.check: The draft says 'staying in the connection once the clearing stops is the work now' — the record only gives the seat (things built on false premises falling away) and the signature (a genuine connection being chosen); it never says something specific was cleared or that a stay is required, so a reader could rightly say 'the clearing already happened and I didn't need to hold anything.' The ask survives my being wrong: knowing which pull is yours is useful whether or not a connection is at stake. The sentence that serves me more than the person is 'the choice keeps getting re-made' — it sounds like a mechanism where the record only shows a chosen direction.
